questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the following idiom: **To fish in troubled waters**

options.label: A
options.text: To engage in adventurous water sports during a storm

options.label: B
options.text: To take advantage of a chaotic or difficult situation for personal gain

options.label: C
options.text: To mediate and resolve conflicts between warring parties

options.label: D
options.text: To deliberately create problems to test someone's patience

questions.solution: **Shortcut (Elimination Technique):** 1. **Eliminate Literal Meanings:** Option A describes a literal physical activity; idioms are metaphorical. Discard A. 2. **Analyze Connotation:** "Troubled waters" implies an existing crisis/chaos. The idiom describes exploiting this state, not resolving it (Option C is positive/altruistic) or creating it from scratch (Option D focuses on causation rather than exploitation). 3. **Select Best Fit:** Option B captures the core nuance: *opportunistic exploitation of a pre-existing crisis*. **Step-by-Step Solution:** The idiom "to fish in troubled waters" originates from the idea that fish are easier to catch when the water is disturbed. Figuratively, it means to try to gain an advantage or profit from a state of confusion, disorder, or crisis. Option B correctly defines this as taking advantage of a chaotic situation for personal gain. Option C is the opposite (resolving). Option D implies the person causes the trouble, whereas the idiom focuses on leveraging existing trouble. Option A is the literal trap.

questions.text: In the following letter series, what should come in place of the question mark? A, C, F, J, O, ?
questions.solution: Shortcut: The gaps between consecutive letters increase by one each time (+2, +3, +4, +5), so the next gap is +6; adding 6 to O gives U. Step‑by‑step: A→C (+2), C→F (+3), F→J (+4), J→O (+5), therefore O→? = O+6 = U.

questions.text: Statements: Only a few Pens are Pencils. All Pencils are Erasers. No Eraser is a Sharpener. Conclusions: I. All Pens can never be Erasers. II. Some Pencils are not Sharpeners. III. Some Pens are not Pencils. Which of the conclusions logically follow?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Translate 'Only a few A are B' into 'Some A are B' + 'Some A are not B'. Use standard Venn rules: All + No = No. 'All Pencils are Erasers' + 'No Eraser is Sharpener' → 'No Pencil is Sharpener' → 'Some Pencils are not Sharpeners' (II True). 'Only a few Pens are Pencils' directly gives 'Some Pens are not Pencils' (III True). For I: Since Some Pens are Pencils and All Pencils are Erasers, Some Pens ARE Erasers, so 'All Pens can never be Erasers' is False. Step-by-step: 1. 'Only a few Pens are Pencils' ⇒ Some Pens are Pencils & Some Pens are not Pencils (III follows). 2. All Pencils are Erasers; No Eraser is Sharpener ⇒ No Pencil is Sharpener ⇒ Some Pencils are not Sharpeners (II follows). 3. Some Pens are Pencils (from stmt 1) and those Pencils are Erasers ⇒ Some Pens are Erasers. Thus 'All Pens can never be Erasers' is false (I fails).

questions.text: As per the Monetary Policy Framework Agreement signed between the Government of India and the RBI (2016), what is the inflation target and the tolerance band mandated for the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC)?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use the '4-2-6' mnemonic: Target 4%, Band ±2%, Range 2%-6%. Options with 5% target are distractors. Full Solution: The RBI Act, 1934 (amended by Finance Act, 2016) mandates the Central Government to set the inflation target in consultation with RBI every 5 years. The current target (2021-2026) is 4% CPI inflation with an upper tolerance limit of 6% and lower limit of 2% (i.e., ±2%). This replaced the earlier multiple indicator approach with a flexible inflation targeting framework.

questions.text: As per the Reserve Bank of India's Scale Based Regulation (SBR) framework for Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs), effective from October 2022, what is the minimum asset size threshold for an NBFC to be classified in the 'Middle Layer' (NBFC-ML)?
questions.solution: (a) Shortcut - Regulatory Hierarchy Elimination: The SBR framework has four layers: Base (<₹1,000 Cr), Middle (≥₹1,000 Cr), Upper (Top 10/Scoring), Top. The Middle Layer is the immediate step up from Base; hence the threshold is exactly the Base Layer ceiling: ₹1,000 Crore. Eliminate ₹500 Cr (Base layer range) and ₹5,000/₹10,000 Cr (specific Upper/Top layer triggers). (b) Full Solution: As per the RBI Circular dated October 22, 2021 (effective Oct 1, 2022), NBFCs are classified into four layers based on asset size, activity, and scoring. NBFC-Base Layer (NBFC-BL): Asset size < ₹1,000 Crore. NBFC-Middle Layer (NBFC-ML): Asset size ≥ ₹1,000 Crore. NBFC-Upper Layer (NBFC-UL): Identified via parametric scoring or top 10 by asset size. NBFC-Top Layer (NBFC-TL): Ideally empty, populated only if systemic risk rises.

questions.text: Rearrange the following four sentences (P, Q, R, S) in the correct sequence to form a coherent paragraph. P: The Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) is mandated to meet at least four times in a year. Q: These meetings are critical as they determine the policy repo rate. R: The decisions taken therein influence liquidity and inflation trajectories across the economy. S: The quorum for such a meeting is four members, including the Governor.
questions.solution: Shortcut (Mandatory Pairs & Pronoun Anchors): 1. 'Such a meeting' in S refers back to 'meet' in P -> **P-S** is a mandatory pair. Eliminate A (PQRS), C (PRSQ), D (SRQP). Only B (PSQR) remains. 2. Verify flow: 'These meetings' (Q) refers to meetings in P/S. 'Therein' (R) refers to meetings in Q. Chain: P-S-Q-R. Step-by-Step: 1. Sentence P introduces the subject (MPC) and the frequency of meetings. 2. Sentence S provides a specific procedural detail ('quorum') about the meeting mentioned in P using the demonstrative phrase 'such a meeting'. This creates a fixed **P-S** block. 3. Sentence Q uses the pronoun 'These meetings', which points back to the meetings described in P and S. Thus Q follows the block -> **PSQ**. 4. Sentence R uses the adverb 'therein' (meaning 'in those meetings'), referring directly to the meetings in Q. It describes the consequence of the decisions made in Q. Thus R concludes the paragraph -> **PSQR**.

questions.text: The length of a rectangle is increased by 20% and its breadth is decreased by 10%. What is the percentage change in the area of the rectangle?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use the successive percentage change formula: Net % change = a + b + (a×b)/100. Here a = +20 (length), b = -10 (breadth). Net change = 20 - 10 + (20×-10)/100 = 10 - 2 = +8% (increase). Full Solution: Let original length = L and breadth = B. Original Area = L×B. New Length = 1.2L, New Breadth = 0.9B. New Area = 1.2L × 0.9B = 1.08 LB. Percentage change = (1.08 - 1) × 100 = 8% increase.

questions.text: As per the RBI's 'Guidelines for Licensing of Payments Banks' (updated April 2021), what is the maximum end-of-day deposit balance that a Payments Bank can hold per individual customer?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Initial limit was ₹1 Lakh (2014). Doubled to ₹2 Lakh in April 2021 to enhance financial inclusion. Eliminate ₹50k (old PPI limit) and ₹5L (SFB/Universal Bank territory). Full Solution: Payments Banks were initially restricted to a maximum deposit balance of ₹1 Lakh per customer. In April 2021, RBI enhanced this limit to ₹2 Lakh per individual customer (end-of-day balance) to allow greater flexibility. They cannot undertake lending activities; deposits must be invested in SLR-eligible G-secs/T-Bills.

questions.text: Five friends A, B, C, D, and E are sitting in a straight line facing north. B sits third to the right of A. C sits immediately to the left of D. E sits at one of the extreme ends. A does not sit at any extreme end. Who sits at the extreme left end?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Since B is third to the right of A and A cannot be at an end, A must be 2nd and B 5th; E takes the only vacant extreme (1st), forcing C and D into 3rd and 4th with C left of D, so the leftmost person is E. Step‑by‑step: Place A at position 2 (only spot allowing B at 5), put B at 5, put E at 1 (the free end), then fill 3 and 4 with C and D respectively because C is immediately left of D.

questions.text: If 'A + B' means 'A is the sister of B', 'A - B' means 'A is the husband of B', 'A * B' means 'A is the son of B', and 'A / B' means 'A is the mother of B', then in the expression 'P * Q - R / S + T', how is P related to T?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Trace the expression from left to right (or right to left) drawing a quick family tree with gender markers. 'P * Q' → P is Son of Q (P=Male). 'Q - R' → Q is Husband of R (Q=Male, R=Female). 'R / S' → R is Mother of S. 'S + T' → S is Sister of T. Thus, R is mother of S and T; Q is father of S and T; P is son of Q, making P brother of S and T. Step-by-step: 1. P * Q: P (Male) → Son of Q. 2. Q - R: Q (Male) → Husband of R. So Q & R are parents. 3. R / S: R → Mother of S. 4. S + T: S → Sister of T. So S & T are siblings, children of Q & R. 5. P is also son of Q. Therefore, P is Brother of T.

questions.text: Under the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY), what is the accidental insurance cover amount available to RuPay debit cardholders for cards issued after August 28, 2018?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Eliminate ₹1 Lakh (pre-2018 cover) and ₹5/₹10 Lakh (confusion with PMJJBY/PMSBY life/accident covers). The PMJDY RuPay cover was doubled to ₹2 Lakh in 2018. Full Solution: The PMJDY scheme initially provided ₹1 Lakh accidental cover. Effective August 28, 2018, the Government enhanced this cover to ₹2 Lakh for new RuPay cardholders. PMJJBY offers ₹2 Lakh life cover for ₹436/yr, and PMSBY offers ₹2 Lakh accident cover for ₹20/yr, but the specific PMJDY RuPay card benefit is ₹2 Lakh.

questions.text: Which of the following sets correctly identifies the three tenors of Treasury Bills (T-Bills) currently issued by the Government of India through the Reserve Bank of India?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Spot the doubling pattern: 91 × 2 ≈ 182, 182 × 2 = 364. Eliminate options with 14-day (discontinued 2001), 273-day, or 728-day (non-standard). Full Solution: The Government of India currently issues three types of T-Bills via RBI auctions: 91-day (weekly), 182-day (weekly), and 364-day (weekly). The 14-day Intermediate T-Bills were discontinued in 2001. T-Bills are zero-coupon securities issued at a discount and redeemed at face value.

questions.text: Rohan starts from his home and walks 12 metres East. He then takes a left turn and walks 5 metres. He again takes a left turn and walks 12 metres. Finally, he takes a right turn and walks 9 metres. What is the straight-line distance (in metres) between his final position and his home?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Track Net North-South and Net East-West displacements separately. Opposite directions cancel out. Net East-West: +12 (East) - 12 (West) = 0. Net North-South: +5 (North) + 9 (North) = 14 (North). Distance = √(0² + 14²) = 14m. Step-by-step: 1. Start (0,0). 2. 12m East → (12,0). 3. Left (North) 5m → (12,5). 4. Left (West) 12m → (0,5). 5. Right (North) 9m → (0,14). 6. Distance from origin (0,0) = √[(0-0)² + (14-0)²]

questions.text: What is the unit digit of the product (6374)^1793 × (625)^317 × (341)^491?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Find unit digit of each base raised to its power using cyclicity. Unit digit of 6374 is 4 (cyclicity 2: 4, 6). Power 1793 is odd → unit digit 4. Unit digit of 625 is 5 → always 5. Unit digit of 341 is 1 → always 1. Multiply unit digits: 4 × 5 × 1 = 20 → unit digit 0. Full Solution: (4^odd) ends in 4. (5^any) ends in 5. (1^any) ends in 1. Product = ...4 × ...5 × ...1 = ...20. Hence, unit digit is 0.

questions.text: Under the Stand Up India Scheme, what is the permissible loan amount range for Greenfield enterprises set up by Scheduled Caste (SC), Scheduled Tribe (ST), or Women entrepreneurs?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Remember '10 to 100' (Lakhs to Crore). It is a composite loan (Term Loan + Working Capital) between ₹10 Lakh and ₹1 Crore. Eliminate lower ranges (MUDRA Shishu/Kishor) and higher ranges (Corporate lending). Full Solution: Stand Up India facilitates bank loans between ₹10 Lakh and ₹1 Crore for at least one SC/ST borrower and one Woman borrower per bank branch for Greenfield projects (manufacturing/services/trading). The loan covers 75% of project cost (up to 85% in some cases) and is repayable in 7 years with 18 months moratorium.
